Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second innings! The umpires are already out to the middle. The Indian players are seen warming up and some of them are carrying out the fielding drills as well. They spread out to the respective fielding positions now. Also, Sarfaraz Khan will be taking the field as a substitute in place of Ravichandran Ashwin for now. For Bangladesh, Zakir Hasan and Shadman Islam are the two openers. And it will be Jasprit Bumrah to kick things off with the new ball for India. And, here we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

India have added just 37 runs to their overnight score losing 4 wickets in the process as well and this is exactly what Bangladesh would have wanted after a torrid final session on Day 1. The sun is shining and it is a typical Chennai day but there is still something in the pitch that Bumrah and co will look to exploit early on. Can the Bangladeshi openers weather the storm and set the platform? Or will India pick up early breakthroughs? We shall find out soon as Bangladesh's first innings is up next.

Day 2 began with India in command and Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja were well set and ready to take on the second new ball. However, Taskin Ahmed came out firing on all cylinders and bowled a lovely spell up top with the second new ball. Taskin removed Jadeja early to expose the lower order but Hasan Mahmud didn't show the same control as he did on Day 1 and Akash Deep racked up a few quick runs. Taskin though continued his good work and picked up a couple of more wickets before Hasan came back and got the final wicket.

Right then, Hasan Mahmud rounds things up for Bangladesh becoming the first player from his country to take a five-wicket haul in India and he also makes it back-to-back five-wicket hauls. India though will be fairly pleased with their effort with the bat, mustering up 376 solid runs thanks to a huge 199-run stand between Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja.

OUT! FINALLY, A FIVE-WICKET HAUL FOR HASAN MAHMUD AS HE WRAPS THE INDIAN INNINGS WITH A HUGE ACHIEVEMENT! Good length ball around the off stump and it deviates away from the batter after pitching. Bumrah is rooted in the crease and approaches it tentatively getting in an awkward position, plays it away from his body and with an angled bat and gets the outside edge that flies straight into the hands of Zakir Hasan stationed at third slip. Hasan Mahmud becomes the first Bangladeshi pacer to achieve a five-wicket haul on Indian soil, and a very well-deserved one.

Commentary.Commentary: Everything happening here! Drama! Also, an appeal for LBW, but the umpire says 'No'. Hasan bowls a well-directed yorker on the stumps, Jasprit Bumrah bends to negotiate the yorker and tries to dig it out to the leg side. He does bring his bat down in time but the ball passes closely to the bat and pings his front pad. The ball then rolls towards behind square on the off side. Meanwhile, the fielder there at the off side picks and throws at the non-striker's end but has a huge shy at it and with no proper backup it results in an overthrow, the ball runs towards the deep mid-wicket fence where the fielder from deep square leg just about manages to pull the ball back with a slide. Now, the question is whether he has nicked the ball before the pad. UltraEdge shows a clear deflection off the bat. Not Out it is and the batters take two in the meantime.

India have done decently to muster up quick runs but 400 seems a bit far away given they have just one wicket in hand and will hope that Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj can hit a few lusty blows here. With that said, Siraj is the last man in for India.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for Day 2 to begin! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of Bangladesh can be seen in a huddle as skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto gives them a final talking to. The pair of Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja is ready to resume their overnight stay at the crease for India. The umpire signals that Bangladesh have taken the second new ball and it will be Taskin Ahmed to begin proceedings with the ball here. Let's go...

PITCH REPORT - Murali Kartik and Dinesh Karthik are inspecting the Day 2 pitch. Dinesh Karthik begins by talking about the weather and says it is sunny and around 30 degrees and will get warmer as the day progresses. Also says that with the heat, it is going to be a good day for the batters. Mentions that Bangladesh must take the new ball from the get-go and make use of the conditions. Reckons that the first half hour will be crucial for the batters and Bangladesh have a massive task ahead of them. Also reckons that this pitch will not break up through the middle. Informs there's a bit of moisture but less than the previous day and ends by saying it should be a superb day for batting.

Typically, we have seen some huge first innings scores in Chennai, so, India's current score shouldn't be a surprise but the pitch is a bit different and the overhead conditions too. Can Bangladesh find a second wind early on Day 2? Or will India continue to dominate the first innings? We shall find out soon as the action isn't far away.

Bangladesh ended Day 1 on the backfoot as they conceded runs heavily and the over rate was quite slow but it is a new day and they will have the option to take the second new ball right away. Hasan Mahmud will be key but the others will have to find a way to step up as well if they are to clean up India quickly on the second morning.

India have the runs on the board they would have wanted after being inserted into bat and they will be eyeing 100 or so more runs to add to the total. Given the way Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja have batted so far, if they negate the second new ball, it could be batting paradise yet again. Also, with his second ton in Chennai, Ashwin became just the fifth player to score multiple tons and take multiple five-fors at the same venue in Test cricket.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test match between India and Bangladesh at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. Day 1 was a humdinger with the visitors staying on top of things for a long time before eventually the hosts rallied back to end the day on top.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, India in the ascendancy at the end of Day 1 but it will be a new day tomorrow and Bangladesh will have the second new ball available right away. Early conditions might be testing for the batters and the visitors will look to strike. India will eye getting close to the 400-run mark and setting things up nicely for their bowlers. Day 2 action begins at 4 am GMT on Friday but you can tune in an hour in advance to our build-up. Cheers!

Not much to write home about Bangladesh and their performance on the field in that final session as they couldn't pick up a single wicket and just succumbed to pressure. Hasan Mahmud had set things up in the first session and then Nahid Rana showed glimpses of greatness in the second session but the two spinners, Mehidy Hasan and Shakib Al Hasan lacked control and couldn't get the job done in the final session with the pacers tiring out.

Generally, Day 1 is the best day for batting at the Chepauk and after aiding the seamers for the first two sessions, the pitch did flatten out and with the sun coming out as well, there was nothing in it for the bowlers. Still, India were in a precarious position but the duo of Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja who have both played a lot at this ground, stitched together a monumental stand with Ashwin finishing the day with a 6th Test ton on his home ground, just a couple of days after his 38th birthday. Jadeja also ended the day on an unbeaten 86 and will look to bring up the three-figure mark as well.

SESSION SUMMARY - 32 overs, 163 runs and 0 wickets! What an end to the first day of play here in Chennai and at the end of it all, hosts India seem to be in complete command which seemed highly unlikely towards the end of the second session. Bangladesh will be deflated after having been ahead in the game for the bulk of Day 1 and will now have to regroup and come back strongly on Day 2.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! Another hour has flown by on Day 1 and this one well and truly belongs to the Indians. Jadeja and Ashwin, the two vastly experienced men and both pretty much well aware of the conditions in Chennai, have played freely and formed a resilient stand together. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of Day 1. The umpires are punctual and the players of Bangladesh spread out to the middle after a huddle talk. Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja walk out to the crease and will resume their innings with the bat for India. Taskin Ahmed (13-1-41-0) to get the proceedings underway after Tea. And, here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Right then, another session has flown by and it has ebbed and flowed back and forth with this match moving at a brisk pace. Coming into the final session, India will aim to go unblemished while Bangladesh will try to restrict India below a challenging total, and look to snag quick wickets as they come out to bowl. Stay tuned as the post-Tea session begins at 9 am GMT.

Bangladesh's efforts were immediately rewarded when Hasan Mahmud struck with the prized scalp of Rishabh Pant, providing an early breakthrough. Nahid Rana complemented Mahmud's efforts well, maintaining both his pace and consistency throughout his spells. The seamers continued to find assistance from the conditions, prompting the Bangladesh think tank to stick with their pace-heavy strategy. They rotated their trio of fast bowlers between Hasan Mahmud, Rana, and Taskin Ahmed - although Taskin struggled at times to find his optimal length. Mehidy Hasan operated from the other end and eventually added his name to the wicket-takers list.

India's innings took an early hit when Rishabh Pant fell victim to a sharp delivery, abruptly ending a promising 62-run partnership and setting a sombre tone for the session. Jaiswal's confidence visibly grew as the session progressed, culminating in a well-deserved half-century. And the arrival of KL Rahul brought much-needed calm to the Indian innings. Partnering with the young and impressive Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rahul helped steer the ship through choppy waters momentarily with a 48-run stand. However, the tide turned once again as both set batters departed in quick succession. With the scoreboard not yet showing a commanding total, the team found itself facing the challenging task of rebuilding. With two new batters at the crease and the ball doing a bit of mischief for the pacers, Jadeja and Ashwin navigated cautiously. Ashwin played some fantastic strokes and kept the scorecard ticking to see India through the session with a brisk partnership.

TEA, DAY 1 - SESSION SUMMARY -  25 overs, 88 runs, 3 wickets. Bangladesh would be very pleased with their bowling efforts going to the dressing room as they have managed to clean up the Indian middle order in this session, quite effectively. Conditions remained pretty much overcast with the sun struggling to pop out of the clouds. And as it is generally said that the second session is the best time to bat on, it certainly wasn't the case this time around. With the residual moisture still present, it helped the pacers to extract some assistance.

Given as runs and that is a dramatic way to end the second session. Hasan Mahmud goes full and straight and looks to swing the ball into the legs. Ravichandran Ashwin comes forward to flick but plays over it a bit and gets in the pads. There is a huge appeal for LBW and all the fielders are stood still as the batters are stranded halfway and eventually do pick up the single. Najmul Hossain Shanto doesn't opt for the review and there might have been an inside edge on that one. That will be TEA ON DAY1!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 1! The umpires are back out in the middle as the players of Bangladesh form a huddle before walking onto the field as well. The duo of Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rishabh Pant is set to resume their stay at the crease for India. Hasan Mahmud to start proceedings with the ball in the new session. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, given how the conditions look and India's batting depth, Bangladesh would not want to take their foot off the pedal in the session after Lunch as the game can get away quickly. India would want the pair of Jaiswal and Pant to carry on for as long as possible and take the sting out of the game for now. An exciting session awaits, so, join us at 6.40 am GMT for the post-Lunch session.

Not an ideal pitch to start on Day 1 in a Test match in India and the hosts were taken aback by the movement in the air and off the deck as well. All three wickets that fell were nicks and certainly, a couple of them could have been avoided. Rohit Sharma did get a beauty but he did struggle against Hasan Mahmud in general. Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill though should have applied themselves better. Yashasvi Jaiswal looked solid from the get-go and with the help of Rishabh Pant, led the fightback for the hosts with an unbeaten stand of 54 runs.

An uncanny day in Chennai where generally conditions are hot and humid but it was overcast and there was some proper bounce given it is a red soil pitch. The Bangladeshi pacers backed their skipper's decision to bowl first as Hasan Mahmud ripped through the Indian top order picking up 3 huge wickets. Taskin Ahmed was a bit on the shorter side and so was Nahid Rana which they will be looking to correct in the next session.

A session that seemed to be heading a hundred percent toward Bangladesh but in the second hour or so, India have looked much better with the bat, and the two left-handers seem to have regained a bit more control. Bangladesh though will still be very pleased and will look for a couple of more wickets right after the break in order to get back on top.
Flat and full now, quicker too, on off, Rishabh Pant makes a quick amend to defend it off the back foot. And that will be LUNCH ON DAY 1.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities now and it is time for the first Test to commence! The two umpires walk out to the middle. The players of Bangladesh scatter through the field and take their respective positions. Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal are the two openers for India and are all geared up and walk out to the pitch. Taskin Ahmed will get the proceedings underway with the shining SG cherry for Bangladesh. And, here we go...

Well then, we are just a few moments away from the action to begin at Chepauk! But before that, the two sets of players are lined up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

Ravichandran Ashwin is down for a quick chat. He says that his excitement and ambition always remain the and enjoys every game of cricket. Adds that age is just a number but you need to be fit and it does take a toll on the long run. Mentions that generally, batters have got huge runs at this ground and it has been a good Test match pitch and with it being a red soil pitch, there will be extra bounce as well. Adds that it was a fine result for Bangladesh with everything going on and they are looking forward to their challenge.

Rohit Sharma, the captain of India says that they would have bowled first as well. Mentions the pitch looks soft and it will be challenging. But also says that they have prepared well and will back their potential. Says looking at the last ten matches, every Test match is going to be important and that they want to focus on what's in front of them. Tells that they had a good preparation leading up to this game. Informs that they are going with three seamers and two spinners.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the captain of Bangladesh says that they will bowl first due to the moisture and will look to use the conditions. Reckons that the first session will help the pacers and goes on to say that they played well against Pakistan but this is a new series. Mentions that the youngsters have done well so far and says that it is the same combination with three seamers and two spin all-rounders.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Shadman Islam, Zakir Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, Litton Das (WK), Mehidy Hasan, Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Nahid Rana.
India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Ravichandran Ashwin, Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep, Mohammed Siraj.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Bangladesh and Najmul Hossain Shanto elects to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Murali Kartik and Dinesh Karthik are inspecting the deck. Dinesh Karthik begins by saying that it is a bit cool and as the day progresses, it will get more warm. Informs that it is a red soil pitch and has some residual moisture underneath, and reckons that it might help the seamers early on and the spinners will come into play very soon. Also thinks that India might go with a three-seamers combination.

With all said and done, this series means a lot from both teams’ perspectives. For India, they would like to make the most out of this home season and sustain their top position in the ongoing cycle of WTC. Whereas, for Bangladesh, currently in the 4th spot of the championship, it’s a huge opportunity to turn the tables and disrupt India’s home record and further better their position in the championship. Stay tuned, as we immerse ourselves in five days of engrossing cricket. Toss and team sheets up next very shortly.

Chepauk has always offered a spin-friendly deck and the wear and tear might see spinners in action pretty soon. The reason, the red soil wicket presumably dries a lot sooner and is prone to break up in the early stages of the game, though it produces a good bounce too for the seamers. But hey, we have seen loads and loads of runs being scored here as we turn the pages to history with 759 being the highest score ever here. The average first inning score here is around the 350-run mark which proves that the batters have enjoyed their strokes as well.

Chennai presents a formidable challenge in September due to its notoriously sweltering conditions. Players can expect to contend with scorching temperatures and stifling humidity using sweatbands and facial creams to combat it. Also, the forecast reckons that there might be a few stoppages here and there in the coming days with some spells of thunderstorms and rains. Despite the gruelling climate, Chepauk has long been a fortress for the Indian team, with a record of 15 victories, 7 defeats, 11 draws, and a memorable tie against Australia in 1986. These punishing weather conditions make Chepauk a tough prospect for any visiting team, particularly during this time of year.

Sure, India at home is a tough team to beat as they have won 17 series since 2013 and have lost just four Tests and are yet to face a series defeat. On paper, India’s team looks bullish but this Bangladesh side has now become habitual and finds dignity in achieving the historic firsts. The visiting team now takes pride in breaking new ground, potentially making them a dark horse threat to India's stellar home record. So, they’re absolutely no walkovers if you think it’s a one-way fight.

Bangladesh storms into this series riding a wave of triumph, still basking in the glory of their historically successful Pakistan tour. This monumental success has not only boosted team morale but has also reshaped perceptions of Bangladesh's capabilities. Building on this newfound momentum, the team, led by Najmul Hossain Shanto, enters this series with an air of confidence and self-belief. The experienced duo of Shakib and Mushfiqur, along with the burgeoning talent of all-rounder Mehidy Hasan, form the backbone of a squad. However, Bangladesh has had to contend with an unexpected setback, the injury to Shoriful Islam. Intriguingly, rather than opting for a like-for-like replacement, they've chosen to bolster their wicket-keeping batter option by including Jaker Ali. Whereas, Nahid Rana, Hasan Mahmud and Taskin Ahmed form their pace trio. And with several spin bowling options along with the experienced Taijul Islam, it rounds up their squad, which looks pretty balanced.

After a six-month hiatus from Test cricket, the Indian team is set to don their whites once again, following their triumphant series against England earlier this year. Led by Rohit Sharma, and with key players like Virat Kohli, Jasprit Bumrah, Siraj and others, the squad aims to strengthen their position in the ongoing cycle World Test Championship. The team composition largely mirrors their previous outing, with the notable additions of KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant, offering a wealth of wicket-keeping batting options. The bowling department sees fresh faces in Yash Dayal and Akash Deep, expanding India's arsenal of pace options as they prepare to take the field. While the Jadeja-Ashwin-Kuldeep-Axar spin quartet will be key in these spin-friendly conditions. With a good blend of youth and experienced energies, team India will aim to dominate their home season on a positive note.
